major_concerns: Verifier soundness and coverage not fully specified (false negatives risk).
Adversarial-intent construction may not reflect real-world malicious operators (external validity).
Risk of repair overconstraint causing availability regressions not measured by security-only metrics.
Device/vendor diversity and emulator fidelity not enumerated; single-testbed bias possible.
required_design_repairs: Specify formal verifier semantics, limits, and proof-of-correctness assumptions; include at least one independent verifier implementation or clear oracle definition.
Define adversarial-intent generation methodology and threat model with examples; justify ecological validity.
Add explicit availability/regression metrics (reachability loss, service impact) and incorporate them into primary outcomes.
Prespecify device/vendor coverage and justify emulator choices; include sensitivity analysis over device profiles.
Detail manual spot-check protocol for verifier false negatives and how repairs are audited.

major_concerns: Legal/ethical risks from real configuration sharing and sanitization may reduce realism.
Annotation workload and inter-annotator agreement plan are underspecified.
Benchmark generalizability across vendors and production networks is limited without explicit device diversity.
Risk of dataset bias if public repo selection criteria or synthetic generation not prespecified.
required_design_repairs: Provide a concrete sanitization/anonymization protocol and legal review checklist prior to release.
Specify annotation guidelines, annotator training, target inter-annotator agreement thresholds, and adjudication process.
Prespecify device/vendor coverage and validation plan; include emulation compatibility matrix.
Publish hosting, licensing, and reproducibility artifacts (VM/container images, seeds, eval scripts) and a minimal compute plan for reproducing published numbers.
Justify sample size and power calculations for the primary ratio outcome.

major_concerns: Emulator fidelity for QoS (hardware queues, shaping) is a major threat to construct validity.
Validator thresholds and traffic profiles are underspecified, risking non-reproducible pass/fail labels.
Iterative repairs can oscillate or degrade other metrics (latency, fairness) which are not fully planned for.
Time-sensitivity and model-call cost trade-offs need clearer stopping rules.
required_design_repairs: Define traffic profiles, simulator/emulator fidelity assumptions, and justify chosen emulator against hardware behavior.
Prespecify QoS metrics (throughput/latency percentiles), validator thresholds, and pass/fail criteria.
Add oscillation detection and mitigation in repair loop (e.g., monotonicity constraints or rollback policy).
Pre-register latency/model-call budgets and measure practical feasibility for time-sensitive ops.
Include sensitivity analysis showing how emulator inaccuracies could affect conclusions.

major_concerns: Adversarial-intent synthesis may be artificial; realism and adversary model need specification.
Device-profile mismatch scenarios are unspecified in scope and may not capture real vendor heterogeneity.
Power to detect interaction effects may be insufficient without a clear power analysis.
Failure-mode taxonomy and labeling methodology are underspecified, risking ambiguous interpretations.
required_design_repairs: Prespecify adversarial-perturbation generation methods, examples, and threat-model justification (human-labeled seed set or adversarial-paraphrase algorithm).
Enumerate device-profile mismatch types and include representative vendor CLIs; justify emulator mappings.
Provide power analysis for interaction detection and set K accordingly; prespecify equivalence bounds.
Define a clear failure-mode taxonomy, annotation protocol, and inter-annotator reliability targets.
Control for confounders (prompt templates, model temperature) and prespecify analysis covariates.
